consensus.title: Off-by-one in full-buffer check allows silent overflow
Negative or zero capacity accepted, crashes later

responses.content:
* [CRITICAL] LOGIC Off-by-one in buffer-full check (in `push`)
  - The condition `self._count > len(self._buf)` allows one extra write past capacity. When `_count == len(self._buf)` the buffer is full but the check passes, so the next `push` overwrites the oldest element and increments `_count` beyond the allocated size. The buffer silently corrupts its own invariant and will eventually raise `IndexError` or lose data.
  - Fix: Change `>` to `>=` so the exception fires exactly when the buffer is at capacity.

* [WARNING] STRUCTURE No read/pop mechanism exposed
  - `_head` advances on every push but there is no `_tail` or `pop` method shown. Once the buffer wraps, previously written items are overwritten with no way to retrieve them. If this is meant to be a general-purpose ring buffer, a `pop`/`read` method and a `_tail` pointer are needed; if it's intentionally write-only, the class name and `BufferFull` exception are misleading.
  - Fix: Add a `pop` method that reads from `_tail`, advances it, and decrements `_count`, or rename the class to reflect write-only semantics.

* [CRITICAL] [LOGIC] RingBuffer.push allows overflow and misdetects full condition (at push)
    - Issue: The condition `if self._count > len(self._buf):` never triggers when the buffer is full, allowing `push` to overwrite existing items and increment `_count` beyond capacity, breaking the buffer invariant. Additionally, `BufferFull` is undefined, causing a `NameError` when the condition would finally trigger.
    - Fix: Define `BufferFull` (e.g., `class BufferFull(Exception): pass`) and change the condition to `if self._count == len(self._buf): raise BufferFull()`.

* [WARNING] LOGIC RingBuffer push allows overflow when buffer full (at push)
    - Issue: The condition `if self._count > len(self._buf):` only raises when count exceeds capacity, allowing a push when count == capacity to overwrite the oldest element and increment count beyond capacity, breaking the buffer invariant.
    - Fix: Change the condition to `if self._count >= len(self._buf): raise BufferFull()`.

* [ERROR_HANDLING] Missing BufferFull exception definition (at push)
    - Issue: The code raises `BufferFull()` but this exception is not defined in the snippet, causing a NameError at runtime when the buffer is full.
    - Fix: Define the exception, e.g., `class BufferFull(Exception): pass`, before the class or import it from an appropriate module.

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC Fullness check (RingBuffer.push)
  - Issue: The fullness check uses `self._count > len(self._buf)`, which permits the buffer to be filled one item beyond capacity, breaking the invariant that `_count <= capacity`. After `capacity` pushes, the next push incorrectly succeeds, overwriting the oldest element without raising `BufferFull`.
  - Fix: Change the condition to `if self._count >= len(self._buf):` (or `self._count == len(self._buf)`) to raise when the buffer is full.

* [CRITICAL] [LOGIC] Off-by-one in full-buffer check allows silent overflow (at `push`)
  - Issue: The condition `self._count > len(self._buf)` permits insertion when `_count == capacity`. For a buffer of capacity 3, the 4th item passes the check: `_count` increments to 4, `_head` wraps, and `_buf[0]` is overwritten. The invariant `_count <= capacity` is violated, `_count` grows unbounded, and `BufferFull` is never raised despite the buffer being full. Any consumer relying on `_count` (e.g., `len()` or `pop`) will see corrupted state.
  - Fix: Change the condition to `if self._count >= len(self._buf): raise BufferFull()`.
* [WARNING] [BOUNDS] Negative or zero capacity accepted, crashes later (at `__init__`)
  - Issue: `[None] * capacity` is valid Python for negative `capacity`, producing an empty list. `_head` stays 0. A subsequent `push` attempts `self._buf[0]`, raising `IndexError` instead of failing fast at construction. This hides invalid configuration until first use and produces a confusing traceback deep in the call stack rather than a clear construction-time error.
  - Fix: Validate `if capacity < 0: raise ValueError("capacity must be non-negative")` in `__init__`.

* [CRITICAL] LOGIC RingBuffer push overflow (in push method)
  - Issue: The guard `if self._count > len(self._buf):` never triggers when the buffer is full because `self._count` can reach `len(self._buf)` without exceeding it, allowing `push` to write past the logical capacity, corrupt `self._count`, and overwrite existing items, producing wrong results that callers will trust.
  - Fix: Replace the condition with `if self._count >= len(self._buf): raise BufferFull()` to reject pushes when the buffer is already full.
